reasons: A states the legal basis the key requires: Civil Code arts. 19 and 145, plus art. 157 on return of property. It puts those in a draft message that does not admit adult consumption, says real-name data does not change who made the purchase, and tells the parent not to confess to having made the top-ups. It also sets realistic expectations (partial refund, court reductions for custody fault) and gives the Tencent minors platform, 12315 and 12345 route. B gives no legal basis at all (misses key points 2 and 3), treats the real-name block as something to work around, and gives up the full-refund claim in the draft. Both miss the 法发〔2020〕17号 art. 9 citation and the WeChat bill complaint route, and both give good prevention advice. A's extra claims (Tencent figures and hotline number) are unverifiable, but B invents case facts in the draft message, so A is clearly stronger.
